page.layout: One printed page, right of the gutter: running head at top, then one text column of full lines, ending with a catchword-like word "modi." at the lower right. No margin notes. Left side of the scan shows the binding and a shelf mark in handwriting, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: etiā in Tusculanæ tertiæ proœmio quæritur:ubi esse quidē nobis igniculos et semina innata uirtu tũ scribit,sed ea celeriter malis morib.opinioni- busq; depravatis, sic extingui,ut nusquā naturæ lumen appareat. cuius mali caussas, ait esse per- uersam educatione parentū & magistrorū,tum lectione poetarū, postremò consuetudine vulgi atq; imperitæ multitudinis. Accedit etiā (quod ipse ignorauit) uitiositas illa ab ipso cŏceptu & ortu cŏtracta, propter primi parentis flagitiū: ita ut cum lacte ipso,immò cū spiritu & uita, er rorē suxisse atq; haufisse uideamur.Est præterea in ipsa mali natura hæc uis,ut plus possit ad cor- rumpendū, quàm bonum ad sanandū & confer- uandū:quemadmodū exiguū ueneni,totū uini ca dū potest inficere: & atramẽti uncia,lactis pon do atrū saccere. Cõsideratis igitur generib.homi num atq; naturis,in cohortādo & suadendo eas sentētias eligemus,quæ naturis eorū sint consen- tanceæ maximè.Doctis & politis laudē & decus, maximeq; ea uirtutū genera quæ in cōmuni ho- minū utilitate tuenda augēdaq; uersantur, pro- ponemus: cuiusmodi sunt, lusticia primùm ipsa, deinde fides, liberalitas,religio,pietas,bonitas, fortitudo,atq; id genus alia, ad hominum societa tem tuendã accommodata.Indoctis uerò & im- peritis,emolumēta,uoluptates, cæteraq; huius- modi.

page.notes: Scan is mirrored on the page edge; the very faint text is show-through and not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "saccere" (likely "sacere" or "saccere"), "lusticia" (likely "iustitia"), "scribit" and "mali" lines are clear. Printing errors left as printed, such as "cum lacte" and "er rorē". The word "modi." at lower right is the line end of the last line, not a catchword.
